title: A Simple Pitched-Roof Extension in Harborne
description: A modest rear-extension design proposal for a family house in Harborne, Birmingham, combining matching brickwork, a tiled roof and rooflights to create a brighter kitchen and dining space.
seoTitle: Small Rear Extension Harborne | Pitched-Roof Design
seoDescription: A small rear-extension design proposal in Harborne, Birmingham, with matching brickwork, rooflights and French doors for brighter everyday living.
alt: Harborne rear-extension design proposal with red brick walls, a tiled lean-to roof, two rooflights and white French doors

children.text: A little more room for everyday life

This design proposal explores how a modest addition to a familiar Birmingham family house could make the kitchen and dining area more comfortable. The emphasis is on a useful extra room, a clear route to the garden and a scale that sits naturally beneath the existing first-floor windows.
A roof and materials that feel at home

Warm red brick and a straightforward tiled lean-to roof give the extension a traditional appearance. White-framed French doors and a separate kitchen window divide the rear elevation into practical openings, while two rooflights introduce daylight further into the room.
Keeping the project manageable

The proposal uses a simple rectangular footprint and familiar materials. These choices provide a sensible starting point for a discussion about scope and budget. Actual construction costs would depend on the measured property, specification and contractor quotations.
Small house extensions in Harborne

A compact extension still deserves careful thought about furniture, storage, daylight and how the new room connects to the existing home. This proposal shows the kind of focused design conversation a homeowner can begin with Hepburn Architects. The image is an architectural visualisation of the proposal; it does not record a completed building.

title: A Compact Kitchen Extension in Kings Heath
description: A simple brick kitchen-extension design proposal for a semi-detached house in Kings Heath, Birmingham, using a compact footprint, a rooflight and sliding doors to connect everyday family space with the garden.
seoTitle: Small Kitchen Extension Kings Heath | Birmingham
seoDescription: Explore a compact kitchen-extension design proposal in Kings Heath, Birmingham, with simple brickwork, a rooflight and garden-facing sliding doors.
alt: Kings Heath kitchen-extension design proposal with red brick, a simple flat roof, rooflight and dark-framed sliding doors

children.text: A practical kitchen and dining space

This Kings Heath design proposal looks at a common ambition: a little more space to cook, eat and spend time together in an ordinary semi-detached home. A compact rear addition creates the setting for a kitchen-diner without making the extension dominate the house or garden.
Straightforward brickwork and a clean roofline

The single-storey design pairs warm brick with a restrained dark roof edge. Garden-facing sliding doors bring light and views into the room, with solid brick at either side. A rooflight offers another source of daylight toward the centre of the proposed space.
Making a smaller footprint work harder

The design focus is on usable space. Positioning a dining table near the garden and keeping circulation clear could make the addition feel generous in daily use. A small patio connects the room to the lawn without turning the whole garden into paving.
Rear-extension design in Kings Heath

For homeowners considering a small kitchen extension in Birmingham, an initial design discussion can establish priorities and test how much extra space is really needed. Budget, existing structure and the particular property would shape the next stage. title: A Small Garden-Facing Extension in Hall Green
description: A compact rear-extension design proposal for a family house in Hall Green, Birmingham, with a traditional gabled roof, soft cream render and French doors creating a welcoming place to dine beside the garden.
seoTitle: Small Rear Extension Hall Green | Birmingham
seoDescription: A traditional small rear-extension design proposal in Hall Green, Birmingham, with a gabled tiled roof, cream render and garden-facing French doors.
alt: Hall Green dining-extension design proposal with cream render, a brick plinth, a tiled gable roof and white French doors

children.text: A small addition with a clear purpose

This Hall Green proposal is centred on a straightforward idea: a comfortable dining space with a view of the garden. The compact single-storey addition sits against an ordinary family house, showing how a smaller extension can have a distinct role without a wholesale transformation.
Traditional proportions and familiar finishes

A simple gabled tiled roof gives the room a recognisable domestic shape. Cream render relates to the existing house, while a low brick plinth connects the extension to the original ground-floor brickwork. White-framed doors and a side window keep the appearance calm and familiar.
Connecting the house and garden

French doors open toward a modest paved terrace, with planting and lawn close to the room. The side window introduces light from another direction and offers a view across the garden. The proposal leaves the adjoining rear part of the house visually separate, giving the extension a manageable, clearly defined scope.
Approachable extension design in Hall Green

Small projects can start with a specific need: space for a dining table, a better garden connection or a more comfortable everyday layout. Hepburn Architects can help homeowners explore those priorities before settling the project scope.
